headline: Anthropic is offering the investment firm Blackstone a yield of more than 10% to fund its latest chip deal, with Blackstone funds set to put $9 billion into the debt, the Financial Times reports.
score_reason: Large $9 billion financing at a double-digit yield for a leading AI lab, reported by the Financial Times and relayed by Reuters, but from unnamed sources and not confirmed by either company.
importance_line: A yield above 10% shows what Anthropic is paying to borrow for computing power, which matters to the lenders and investors weighing AI companies' debts, but the terms rest on unnamed sources and the Reuters account carries no comment from either company.
summary: The Financial Times reports, as relayed by Reuters and citing people familiar with the matter, that Anthropic is offering Blackstone, the large US investment firm, a yield (the yearly return paid to a lender) of more than 10% to pay for its latest chip deal, with Blackstone funds to invest $9 billion in debt secured on Anthropic's five-year lease payments for the chips. Our 3 Oct 2026 edition carried a Bloomberg report that Blackstone would commit $9 billion to a riskier slice of a $60 billion chip financing linked to Broadcom, and the Reuters account does not say whether this is the same deal.
notes: FT original paywalled; text read is Reuters' two-sentence relay. url is the FT article link without its tracking code. Possible link to the 3 Oct Bloomberg report is flagged in the summary, not asserted.
